user_text: Plan a 1-day migration from SVN to Git for a small repo.
assistant_text:
# 1-Day SVN → Git Migration Plan

## Pre-Work (Night Before)
- [ ] Install `git-svn` or `svn2git`
- [ ] Audit SVN repo size and history depth
- [ ] Notify team: **SVN freeze starts at 9 AM**

---

## Morning (9 AM – 12 PM)

### 9:00 – Create Authors File
Map SVN usernames → Git identities:
```bash
svn log ^/ --xml --quiet | grep author | sort -u | \
  perl -pe 's/.*>(.*?)<.*/$1 = $1 <$1\@company.com>/' > authors.txt
```
Edit `authors.txt` manually to fill real names/emails.

### 9:30 – Clone SVN Repo
```bash
git svn clone https://svn.example.com/repo \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  --stdlayout \          # assumes trunk/branches/tags
  --no-metadata \
  -s my-repo
```
> ⏱ This may take 1–3 hours for large histories

### 10:00 – (While cloning) Set Up Remote Git Repo
- Create bare repo on GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket
- Configure branch protection rules
- Add team members

---

## Midday (12 PM – 1 PM) — Lunch Break / Clone Finishes

---

## Afternoon (1 PM – 4 PM)

### 1:00 – Clean Up & Convert
```bash
cd my-repo

# Convert svn:ignore → .gitignore
git svn show-ignore > .gitignore
git add .gitignore && git commit -m "Add .gitignore from SVN"

# Convert remote tracking branches to local
for branch in $(git branch -r | grep -v tags | grep -v trunk); do
  git branch ${branch##*/} $branch
done

# Convert tags
for tag in $(git branch -r | grep tags); do
  git tag ${tag##*/tags/} $tag
done
```

### 2:00 – Push to Remote
```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/org/my-repo.git
git push origin --all
git push origin --tags
```

### 2:30 – Verify
- [ ] Commit count matches SVN (`git log --oneline | wc -l`)
- [ ] All branches present
- [ ] All tags present
- [ ] Latest files match SVN working copy
- [ ] CI/CD pipeline runs green

### 3:00 – Team Onboarding
```bash
# Each developer runs:
git clone https://github.com/org/my-repo.git
```
- [ ] Share Git workflow guide (branching strategy, PR process)
- [ ] Update CI/CD configs to point to Git
- [ ] Update any webhook/deploy scripts

---

## End of Day (4 PM – 5 PM)

- [ ] **Archive SVN repo** (read-only, don't delete yet)
- [ ] Update internal docs/wikis
- [ ] Send team announcement: Git is now canonical
- [ ] Schedule 1-week SVN decommission date

---

## Rollback Plan
> If something goes wrong before 3 PM:
> - Re-enable SVN write access
> - Delete Git remote repo
> - Reschedule migration

---

## Key Tools
| Tool | Use |
|------|-----|
| `git svn` | Built-in, reliable |
| `svn2git` | Cleaner branch/tag handling |
| `git log --oneline` | Verify history |

## Top 3 Migration Risks

### 1. 🕐 History Conversion Takes Too Long
**Risk:** Large repos with thousands of commits can take 4–8+ hours to clone via `git svn`, blowing past the 1-day window.
**Mitigation:** Do a trial run the night before; limit history with `--revision HEAD:1` in reverse if needed.

---

### 2. 👤 Incomplete Authors Mapping
**Risk:** Unknown SVN usernames cause the clone to **fail mid-way** or produce commits with broken identities.
**Mitigation:** Fully validate `authors.txt` before starting; add a catch-all with `--authors-prog` fallback script.

---

### 3. 🔗 Broken CI/CD & Integrations
**Risk:** Pipelines, deploy scripts, and webhooks still pointing at SVN silently fail or deploy stale code.
**Mitigation:** Audit all integrations beforehand; update and test CI/CD in parallel before cutting over.

## Migration Checklist

**Prep**
- [ ] Freeze SVN commits
- [ ] Run trial clone to estimate time
- [ ] Validate `authors.txt` is complete

**Migration**
- [ ] Clone SVN → Git with full history
- [ ] Convert branches and tags
- [ ] Add `.gitignore` from `svn:ignore`
- [ ] Push to remote

**Verify**
- [ ] Commit count matches
- [ ] Branches and tags present
- [ ] CI/CD pipeline passes

**Cutover**
- [ ] Update all integrations/webhooks
- [ ] Team clones new repo
- [ ] Set SVN to read-only
If the migration fails, **re-enable SVN write access** and instruct the team to continue working there while you reschedule the migration.
**`git-svn` must be installed** on the machine running the migration.

assistant_text: The **project or engineering lead** should approve the final cutover.
Send a team-wide message the day before with the exact SVN freeze time and Git repo URL.

## Final Recap

- **Goal:** Migrate SVN → Git in one day
- **Key Steps:** Freeze → Clone → Clean up → Push → Verify → Cutover
- **Top Risks:** Long clone time, broken author mapping, broken CI/CD
- **Tools:** `git svn`, `svn2git`
- **Approval:** Engineering lead signs off on cutover
- **Rollback:** Re-enable SVN write access if needed
- **Done:** SVN set to read-only, team on Git

- Freeze SVN early

- Push to remote, test CI/CD
- Lead approves cutover
- Archive SVN, team onboards Git
